note:
Ten floors of Ascendant devotion that rendered as a three-box stack on the shared asc_shrine arm. Built as a ZIGGURAT: seven square boxes stepping in from the podium to a tenth of its width, with a faceted drum lantern on the apex — the one silhouette in Coldwater that narrows the whole way and ends in a point rather than a lid. ⚠ NO AUTHORED `neon`, deliberately. `derivedStyle` reads `m.neon` as a TRUTH TEST for works-vs-front-vs-block, so authoring a colour here would reclassify a stone shrine as a SHOPFRONT and hang a retail kit on it; the accent it wants (#7fc8ff, off the stone family) is what `accentOf` already derives with the field left empty. RENDER_TUNE.legacyArms puts the asc_shrine arm back.

⚠ RESTORED TO THE HEIGHT OF ITS ARM (2026-09-17). The form above is unchanged and was
never the problem; what did not carry across from the asc_shrine arm was how tall it stands. It was
at 71% — 1.06x the storey stack against the arm's 1.50x — so every 'h'-tagged field
here was multiplied by 1.415 and every 'fh'-tagged one left alone. The silhouette is identical;
only the storeys are taller. Same regression as halcyontowers and thespire, same measurement.

⚠ AND THE UPLINK BEAM CAME BACK WITH THE HEIGHT. The asc_shrine arm ran a glowing Ascendant-blue
wire from the cap at 1.5 to 2.6 with a beacon on the end of it, and a server-rack glow on the
Curtain side — the whole reason the building reads as a shrine to a machine rather than as a
black ziggurat. None of it survived the port: this model emitted three sprites on a palette of
[20,28,44], which after dark is nothing at all. The beam is a helixRunner with r0 = r1 = 0 and
turns = 0, which is a straight vertical line through the same emitLightRunner the arm used.

⚠ THE UPLINK WAS A STROKE AND READ AS A SCRATCH ON THE GLASS (2026-09-22). The beam restored above
is a helixRunner with r0 = r1 = 0 through emitLightRunner, which is a STROKE: a length in the world
and a width in SCREEN PIXELS, so the shaft was the same hairline from the next street and from
directly underneath it, and no alpha was ever going to make a line look like light. That is
lightBeam's own header, learned on the lighthouse and then on Voltage, and this was the third
instance of it. It is two skyBeam cones now — widths in TILES, so they open out along their own
length and swell as you close on them, additive and depth-tested through the sprite layer, so the
lantern cuts them per pixel.

⚠ THEY GO STRAIGHT UP AND DO NOT SWEEP (tilt PI/2, sweep 0), which is the difference between this
and Voltage. A club's beams rake the sky because a club is advertising; a shrine is not, and a pair
of fixed verticals reads as a marker rather than as a pitch. The period is still authored because
skyBeam's motion gate is what answers -1 at RENDER_TUNE.motion 0, and at sweep 0 that phase moves
nothing — the beams are already standing still.

⚠ AND THE ZIGGURAT HAD NO EDGES IN IT. Seven setbacks, a drum lantern, a canopy, two bollards and
an antenna cluster, every one of them ty_asc_shrine [20,28,44] — so the silhouette this model was
built for could not be seen at all, and the building read as a black smudge among articulated
frontages. The glass stays black, because that IS the shrine; what it gains is a chrome band on
each setback (ty_asc_chrome_dk, ty_asc_chrome at the lantern collar), which is the one thing a
stepped monument is read by, and the entrance fittings in the same metal so there are three more
parts you can find. No mass moved and no segment changed.
